title: Unit and counit for the rational projective line
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$ and a field $k$ of characteristic $p>0$, $p\ne\ell$, and let $Y$ be a separated finite-type $k$-scheme, in the geometric standing setting [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting]. Fix a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ inside $\Qlb=\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$. Use the continuous-function condensed ring $\underline E$ of [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring] and the finite-subextension-valued condensed ring $\underline{\Qlb}$ of [sk-def-sfb-qlbar-condensed], pulled back to each scheme as in [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients]. Use the ordinary unbounded derived categories of module objects over the pulled-back coefficient sheaves, with derived pullback and direct image [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull], derived tensor [sk-def-sfb-derived-tensor-hom], and Tate twists [sk-def-sp-tate-twist]. Here $\Dbc(X,\Lambda)$ is the full subcategory of bounded complexes whose cohomology admits a finite stratification by constructible locally closed subschemes with finite constant local models: on a pro-etale cover of each stratum a cohomology module is $\Lambda_U\otimes_{\Lambda(*)}V$ for a finitely presented scalar module $V$, as in [sk-def-sfb-constructible], and $\Loc(\Dbc)$ is the smallest full replete triangulated subcategory containing $\Dbc$ and closed under all small ambient coproducts, using the localizing-closure operation of [sk-def-localizing-closure] for these fixed coefficient sheaves.

Let $\Lambda=E$ or $\Qlb$, $q:P=\mathbf P^1_Y=\mathbf P(\{0,1\};Y)\to Y$ [def-nagata-projective-space-base-change], $W=P\times_YP$ with
projections $p_1,p_2:W\to P$ and diagonal $\Delta:P\to W$, and let
$\delta_\Lambda:\Delta_*\Lambda_P\to\Lambda_W(1)[2]$ and
$\operatorname{Tr}_q:Rq_*\Lambda_P(1)[2]\to\Lambda_Y$ be the morphisms of
[det-prop-diagonal-tower-trace] and [det-prop-diagonal-tower-coefficients]. All functors below are the restrictions to the
categories $\Loc(\Dbc(-,\Lambda))$.

1. For $M\in\Loc(\Dbc(P,\Lambda))$ there is a natural isomorphism
   $\Delta_*M\simeq p_1^*M\otimes^{\mathbf L}\Delta_*\Lambda_P$.
2. The *unit* $\eta_M:M\to q^*Rq_*M(1)[2]$ is the composite
   $$
   M=Rp_{2*}\Delta_*M\simeq Rp_{2*}(p_1^*M\otimes^{\mathbf L}\Delta_*\Lambda_P)
   \xrightarrow{Rp_{2*}(1\otimes\delta_\Lambda)}Rp_{2*}\bigl(p_1^*M(1)[2]\bigr)
   \xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }q^*Rq_*M(1)[2],
   $$
   the last arrow being the inverse of the proper base change isomorphism
   $q^*Rq_*\to Rp_{2*}p_1^*$ for the cartesian square formed by $p_1,p_2,q,q$.
3. The *counit* $\varepsilon_K:Rq_*q^*K(1)[2]\to K$ for
   $K\in\Loc(\Dbc(Y,\Lambda))$ is the composite of the projection formula
   isomorphism $Rq_*q^*K(1)[2]\simeq K\otimes^{\mathbf L}Rq_*\Lambda_P(1)[2]$
   with $1\otimes\operatorname{Tr}_q$.

Both are natural transformations of exact functors on these localizing
categories.

proof.text: Geometry and coefficient convention. The projection $q$ is proper by [lemma-nagata-projective-space-base-change-proper]. Each $p_i$ is itself the projective-line projection over $P$, after the canonical identification of the two factors, so the same statement applies over $P$. In particular $q$ is separated, and its diagonal $\Delta$ is closed by the definition in [def-weil-proper-morphism]. The schemes $Y,P,W$ are Noetherian by successive applications of [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian]: first apply it to $Y\to\operatorname{Spec}k$, since a field has only the ideals $0$ and $k$; then apply it to $q:P\to Y$ and to $p_1:W\to P$, which are of finite type because they are proper. Also $\Delta$ is proper by clause (a) of [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-proper]. For each $X\in\{Y,P,W\}$, choose a finite affine open cover of $X$ by spectra of Noetherian rings, using its locally Noetherian and quasi-compact definition. Each chart is a Noetherian topological space by [lem-sc-affine-noetherian-underlying-space]. Every open subset of such a chart is quasi-compact: a cover with no finite subcover would yield a strictly increasing sequence of finite unions of opens, contrary to the ascending chain condition. The intersection of any open subset of $X$ with each of its finitely many charts is therefore quasi-compact, so that open subset is quasi-compact. In particular $Y,P,W$ are qcqs, since each is quasi-compact and every intersection of affine opens is quasi-compact. The structure map $a_Y:Y\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is separated and of finite type by hypothesis. Apply clause (e) of [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence] first to $q$ and $a_Y$, and then to $p_1$ and $a_Yq$: since proper maps are separated and locally of finite type, the structure maps $a_P=a_Yq$ and $a_W=a_Yqp_1$ are separated and locally of finite type. Their quasi-compactness can be checked directly: the only open subsets of $\operatorname{Spec}k$ are the empty set and the whole space, whose inverse images are empty or the quasi-compact schemes $P,W$. Thus both structure maps are of finite type by [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. This proves that $P,W$, as well as $Y$, satisfy the standing separated-finite-type hypothesis of every rational theorem below; all the displayed arrows are $k$-morphisms by construction. Define $j:W\setminus\Delta(P)\hookrightarrow W$ to be the complement inclusion. For every affine open $V$ of $W$, $j^{-1}(V)=V\setminus\Delta(P)$ is quasi-compact, so $j$ is a quasi-compact morphism. This checks the quasi-compact-morphism hypothesis of the open--closed statements. The integer $\ell$ is a unit on $Y,P,W$ and the open complement, since its image is nonzero in the field $k$ of characteristic $p\ne\ell$ and the image of a unit under every structural ring map is a unit. Thus the invertibility hypothesis for the Tate-twist comparisons is satisfied. The chosen $E$ is a finite subextension of the fixed $\Qlb$, and the latter has the finite-subextension-valued convention required by the current coefficient statement. All coefficient rings are the pulled-back condensed ring sheaves, not discrete constant rational sheaves: [sk-prop-sfb-cartesian-coefficients] identifies their inverse images and their twists with the corresponding coefficient sheaves. In particular module pullback is exact inverse image.

source.place: Well-definedness (1): closed diagonal and coefficient system; geometric hypotheses: Stacks Tags 01KU (schemes-lemma-separated-permanence), 01T3 (morphisms-lemma-composition-finite-type), 01W5 (morphisms-lemma-closed-immersion-proper)

proof.text: Domains of the functors. The category $\Dbc$ in this statement uses the finite constant local models of [sk-def-sfb-constructible]: on each stratum its cohomology is locally obtained from a finitely presented scalar module by extension to the coefficient sheaf, and cohomology vanishes outside a finite interval. For these constant-model categories, [det-def-localizing-closure-ctf-equals-bc] identifies $\Dctf$ with $\Dbc$ and their localizing closures. Its qcqs hypothesis holds for $Y,P,W$ by Step 1. Thus these are precisely the categories $\Loc(\Dctf)$ used in the enclosing unit. Pullbacks preserve these closures and are exact by [det-proper-base-change-unbounded-pullback]. Proper pushforwards preserve them and are exact by [det-proper-image-localizing-proper], including $Rq_*,Rp_{i*},R\Delta_*$. Closure under derived tensor is [det-thm-sf-pf-field-tensor]. The coefficient sheaf is a rank-one free module, and the Tate sheaf is locally free of rank one by [sk-def-sp-tate-twist], so each has the finite constant local model with scalar module $\Lambda(*)$ on a single stratum in [sk-def-sfb-constructible]: on a trivializing cover the model is $\Lambda_U\otimes_{\Lambda(*)}\Lambda(*)\simeq\Lambda_U$. The scalar module $\Lambda(*)$ is free of rank one over itself, hence finitely presented. Concentrated in degree zero, they therefore belong to $\Dbc$. Consequently tensoring by the Tate sheaf and shifting also preserve these closures. This checks the domain of each object in all three displayed constructions, including unbounded objects in the localizing closure.

source.place: Well-definedness (1)--(3): restriction to the localizing categories

proof.text: Open and closed restrictions detect isomorphisms even on unbounded complexes. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-ringed-open-closed] with $X=W$, $i=\Delta$ and ring sheaf $\Lambda_W$. It supplies exact $\Delta_*,j_!$, the identities $\Delta^*\Delta_*\simeq1$, $j^*\Delta_*=0$, and the module sequence $0\to j_!j^*F\to F\to\Delta_*\Delta^*F\to0$. By [sk-prop-sfb-cartesian-coefficients] the two inverse images are exact too. Thus they act on cohomology sheaves. If $\Delta^*C=j^*C=0$ for an arbitrary complex $C$, then the exact sequence applied to each $H^nC$ has zero outer terms, hence $H^nC=0$ for every integer $n$. Applying this observation to the cone of a morphism proves joint conservativity. Exact sheaf functors induce triangulated functors by [lem-sf-exact-functor-derived-triangulated]; [sk-def-sfb-derived-categories] also identifies the exact closed pushforward with $R\Delta_*$. No assertion about geometric stalks detecting all pro-etale sheaves is needed.

Diagonal tensor identification, with its actual map. Put $A_M=p_1^*M\otimes^{\mathbf L}\Delta_*\Lambda_P$. The tensor-pullback isomorphism of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback], the pullback composition comparison of [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-derived-pullback-composition], and the identities $p_1\Delta=1$ and $\Delta^*\Delta_*\Lambda_P=\Lambda_P$, identify $\Delta^*A_M$ with $M\otimes^{\mathbf L}\Lambda_P=M$. The same tensor-pullback isomorphism gives $j^*A_M=0$ because $j^*\Delta_*\Lambda_P=0$. Use the derived pullback/direct-image adjunction of [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull] to form its unit $a_M:A_M\to\Delta_*\Delta^*A_M=\Delta_*M$. After $\Delta^*$ it is an isomorphism: the triangle identity composes it with the invertible closed counit to give $1$. After $j^*$ it is the map $0\to0$. The identities and closed counit here are supplied by [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-ringed-open-closed], termwise on complexes as in the preceding step. Joint conservativity from Step 3 makes $a_M$ an isomorphism. Define the isomorphism in clause (1) to be $a_M^{-1}$. It is natural in $M$, since $a$ is an adjunction unit followed by natural tensor and pullback identifications.

source.place: Well-definedness (1): construction and invertibility of the diagonal tensor map

proof.text: The initial identification in the unit. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pushforward-composition] to $P\xrightarrow{\Delta}W\xrightarrow{p_2}P$, with the pulled-back coefficient rings. Since $p_2\Delta=1_P$, it gives $Rp_{2*}R\Delta_*\simeq R(1_P)_*=1$. Here $R\Delta_*=\Delta_*$ by exactness from [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-ringed-open-closed] and the exact-functor clause of [sk-def-sfb-derived-categories]. This is a natural identification for every unbounded $M$. Use its inverse to write $M\simeq Rp_{2*}\Delta_*M$, followed by $Rp_{2*}(a_M^{-1})$.

Base change for the final arrow. The cartesian square has $f=q$, $f'=p_2$, $g=q$, $g'=p_1$. Its canonical exchange map $\beta_M:q^*Rq_*M\to Rp_{2*}p_1^*M$ is the unit--pullback-comparison--counit composite of [def-weil-pbc-ambient-ringed-exchange]. To apply the bounded rational theorem with its general ring-object constructibility convention, take any constant-model $M\in\Dbc(P,\Lambda)$. On every stratum its cohomology has a finite constant local model, hence is locally finitely presented over the coefficient ring object by the final inclusion of [det-def-sfb-constructible-local-model]. The same finite stratification therefore witnesses constructibility in [sk-def-sfb-bounded-constructible], with the same finite cohomological bounds. Consequently $M$ belongs to the bounded category of [det-thm-sfb-proper-base-change-rational], and clause (3) makes its canonical $\beta_M$ an isomorphism. This uses only the inclusion from constant-model constructibility into ring-object constructibility. By [det-def-localizing-closure-ctf-equals-bc] the constant-model $\Dbc$ objects are exactly the $\Dctf$ generators. The extension statement [det-proper-base-change-unbounded-extension] therefore makes this same $\beta_M$ an isomorphism for every $M\in\Loc(\Dbc(P,\Lambda))$. The properness and closure-preservation hypotheses were checked in Steps 1 and 2. Invert $\beta$ as a natural isomorphism; its direction is $Rp_{2*}p_1^*\to q^*Rq_*$, as required by clause (2).

source.place: Well-definedness (2): proper base change on the localizing closure

proof.text: Finish the unit, including the twist. The rational class $\delta_\Lambda$ exists by [det-prop-diagonal-tower-coefficients], from the tower and trace of [det-prop-diagonal-tower-trace]. Tensor it with $1_{p_1^*M}$ and apply $Rp_{2*}$ to obtain the middle arrow in clause (2). To identify its target, apply the Tate-twist clause of [sk-prop-sfb-cartesian-coefficients] to $p_2:W\to P$, with $d=1$ and $\Lambda=E$ or $\Qlb$. Both schemes have $\ell$ invertible by Step 1, and these are precisely the condensed coefficients specified there; the additional annihilation condition concerns only finite rings and is not needed here. This identifies $\Lambda_W(1)$ with $p_2^*\Lambda_P(1)$. Apply [det-thm-sf-pf-field-localizing] to $p_2$, $A=p_1^*M$ and $B=\Lambda_P(1)$, and shift by $[2]$, to get $Rp_{2*}(p_1^*M(1)[2])\simeq(Rp_{2*}p_1^*M)(1)[2]$. Then apply $\beta_M^{-1}(1)[2]$ from Step 6. This specifies the shift and twist implicit in the final base-change arrow. Combining with Steps 4 and 5 gives exactly $\eta_M:M\to q^*Rq_*M(1)[2]$ with the displayed order of arrows.

source.place: Well-definedness (2): tensoring the diagonal class and twisted proper base change

proof.text: Construct the counit. Set $A=\Lambda_P(1)[2]$ and $B=K$ in [det-thm-sf-pf-field-localizing] for the proper map $q$. Tensor symmetry and $q^*K\otimes^{\mathbf L}\Lambda_P(1)[2]=q^*K(1)[2]$ rewrite the inverse projection isomorphism as $Rq_*q^*K(1)[2]\simeq K\otimes^{\mathbf L}Rq_*\Lambda_P(1)[2]$. The trace of [det-prop-diagonal-tower-trace], extended to $\Lambda=E,\Qlb$ by [det-prop-diagonal-tower-coefficients], gives $1_K\otimes\operatorname{Tr}_q$ into $K\otimes^{\mathbf L}\Lambda_Y\simeq K$. Define $\varepsilon_K$ to be this composite. All these arrows lie in the full localizing subcategories checked in Step 2.

source.place: Well-definedness (3): the projection-formula and trace composite

proof.text: Naturality and exactness. Each unit constituent is natural in $M$: for $u:M\to M'$ the middle tensor square commutes because $(p_1^*u\otimes1)\circ(1\otimes\delta_\Lambda)=(1\otimes\delta_\Lambda)\circ(p_1^*u\otimes1)$ with the respective sources and targets. The other squares are naturality of the adjunction unit, the composition comparison, and the exchange transformation already used. Pasting gives $q^*Rq_*(u)(1)[2]\circ\eta_M=\eta_{M'}\circ u$. For $v:K\to K'$, bifunctoriality gives $(v\otimes1)\circ(1\otimes\operatorname{Tr}_q)=(1\otimes\operatorname{Tr}_q)\circ(v\otimes1)$, and naturality of the projection map gives $v\circ\varepsilon_K=\varepsilon_{K'}\circ Rq_*q^*(v)(1)[2]$. Exactness and shift compatibility of derived tensor and the canonical projection transformation are supplied by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-projection-mate-exact]; pullbacks and the proper pushforwards are exact by [det-proper-base-change-unbounded-pullback] and [det-proper-image-localizing-proper]. Together with the exact shift functor $[2]$ on the derived category [sk-def-sfb-derived-categories], these facts make the source and target functors of $\eta$ and $\varepsilon$ exact. The naturality equations just proved therefore give the asserted natural transformations of exact functors on the stated localizing categories. The names unit and counit specify candidate adjunction maps here; the triangle identities are the separate node det-prop-p1-adjunction-rational-triangle and are not assumed in this construction.

source.place: Final sentence: natural transformations of exact functors

proof_origin.place: Well-definedness (1)--(3), expanded open--closed support argument and explicit functor domains

split_report.summary: Repair of the returned domain and geometric-hypothesis faults. Defines Dbc by finite constant local models (sk-def-sfb-constructible), so ctf=bc applies on exactly the unit domain. Step 6 explicitly embeds these generators in the general ring-object bounded category using the local-model inclusion, before applying bounded rational base change and its unbounded extension. Step 1 cites existing composition permanence for separated and locally finite-type morphisms and checks quasi-compactness over Spec k directly, proving P and W are standing schemes; it cites closed-immersion properness for Delta. All five previously omitted off-unit tools and the inclusion are declared. The nine-step construction and canonical exchange map are retained, with no new nodes.
split_report.blueprint: Realizes step 1 of sk-prop-p1-adjunction-rational and every sentence of the node proof: support and joint conservativity (steps 3--4), composition (5), proper base change (6--7), projection formula and trace (8), naturality/exactness (9); steps 1--2 verify the hypotheses and domains. Triangle identities remain in the sibling node.

tool_uses.why: Properness of projective space is a generic geometric tool needed to apply the unit route; no node of the adjunction unit supplies it.
Generic Noetherian permanence checks the quasi-compact-complement hypothesis of the support argument.
Identifies the rational constructible generators with finite-Tor constructible generators for the cited localizing base-change statements.
Gives precisely the arbitrary-ring-sheaf closed/open identities and exact sequence needed for the support argument; finite constant-coefficient recollement is insufficient.
Generic descent of exact sheaf functors to all unbounded derived categories, used to justify the support/cone test.
Generic monoidality of derived ringed-topos pullback computes both restrictions of the diagonal tensor object.
Generic composition theorem on ordinary unbounded module categories identifies the initial term; bounded scalar-localized comparison theorems would not cover Loc.
Supplies exactness and shift compatibility of tensor and the canonical projection transformation on arbitrary ringed sites.
Generic composition comparison for exact Cartesian-coefficient pullbacks computes Delta^*p_1^*M from p_1 Delta=identity on the unbounded ambient category.

Converts the finite Noetherian affine cover to Noetherian topological charts, so every affine preimage under the open complement inclusion is quasi-compact; the adjunction unit has no separate geometric lemma for this.
Exact Cartesian module inverse image and its Tate-twist comparison are generic coefficient tools; the adjunction unit does not prove them.
Preserves the constant-model Dctf localizing categories and gives exact pullback; the adjunction unit needs this domain theorem.
Proper image preserves the same localizing categories for E and Qlb; this verifies the domains of q, p_i and Delta.

Clause (3) proves invertibility of the canonical exchange on bounded generators, using the explicit inclusion into its ring-object bounded category; the unit has no separate bounded base-change theorem.
Extends that same unit-comparison-counit exchange isomorphism from Dctf to its localizing closure, as required by the unbounded adjunction route.
Its stated inclusion from finite constant local models into locally finitely presented ring-object modules licenses the bounded theorem on the generators; no equality of the two notions is used.
Generic closed-immersion properness is used for the diagonal to apply proper-image preservation.
Clause (e) is the existing composition stability for separated and locally finite-type morphisms needed to verify P and W are standing schemes.
